Optimize the customer decision before monetizing it

Customer problem: fund an obligation without unnecessary conversion or reserve depletion. IPE compares eligible funding and service tiers before recommending a route.

Commercial trade-off: transparent advice may support adoption, retention and relationship value over time. These are hypotheses, not verified outcomes or a forecast.

Client decision → modeled product utilization → potential provider economics. This is one scenario, not observed adoption or revenue.

Payment fee opportunity

Illustrative gross fee assumption per payment. Provider costs, revenue recognition and contribution are not modeled.

FX economics

Modeled markup on the conversion alternative, not realized spread revenue or profit. Principal is not revenue.

Customer value

Reserve preservation and transparent cost/speed choices make the decision inspectable. No realized savings or delivery guarantee is claimed.

Merchant economics boundary

The invoice principal is EUR 750,000. Payment and FX fees are funding costs, not additional merchant invoice proceeds.

Acquiring fees, interchange, processing costs and merchant margin are not modeled.

Potential proposition: embedded workflow licensing

Help a business see invoice readiness, the funding prerequisite and outstanding principal in one workflow. Licensing is a hypothesis requiring merchant demand, integration costs and willingness-to-pay evidence. The synthetic principal does not establish provider revenue.

1 · Treasury intelligence

Client need: Know which funds can safely meet an obligation.

Product behavior: Reserve-aware account visibility and funding comparisons.

Monetization hypothesis: Subscription or embedded licensing.

Validate: Repeated use, willingness to pay and cost to serve.

2 · Transparent payment service tiers

Client need: Balance urgency against payment cost.

Product behavior: Explain standard and priority eligibility.

Monetization hypothesis: Service-tier pricing.

Validate: Urgent payment demand and delivery costs.

3 · FX optimization and relationship economics

Client need: Avoid unnecessary currency conversion.

Product behavior: Compare existing currency with conversion.

Monetization hypothesis: Relationship value versus conversion markup.

Validate: Client value, retention and total relationship economics.

4 · Embedded merchant workflows

Client need: Understand readiness and outstanding invoices.

Product behavior: Connect shared intent with distinct synthetic collection outcomes.

Monetization hypothesis: Workflow licensing.

Validate: Merchant demand, willingness to pay and integration economics.
